hints: Two questions have to be answered in constant time: where is this key, and which entry is the least recently used?
A hash map answers the first. For the second you need the entries in recency order, with the ability to move one to the front in constant time.
An array cannot do that - moving an element shifts everything. A doubly linked list can: unlink a node and relink it at the front, both in constant time.
So the map stores key to *node*, not key to value, and the list holds the entries from most recent to least. Eviction is the last node.
